creative_originality.evidence: The whole idea is an opacity fade: t=0.00 empty, t=0.45 the complete wordmark in flat mid-grey, t=0.88 near-black, t=1.33 full black. Letters, dots and joins never move independently, so the same clip would fit any logo in any script. Nothing comes from the Arabic forms.

motion_quality.evidence: The fade is clean and artefact-free, but it is over by about 1.33s. Frames t=1.77 to t=3.98 (roughly 2.6s, two thirds of the clip) are identical static holds. No easing, overlap or secondary motion is visible, and the dead tail makes the pacing feel unfinished.

brand_relevance.evidence: Nothing contradicts a 'next-generation marketing studio', but nothing expresses it either. The fade is neutral and ignores right-to-left reading, the kashida stretch and the dot system. The wordmark appears all at once instead of being written or built.

visual_clarity.evidence: Every frame from t=0.45 on shows the complete, correctly joined, correctly dotted word, centred with generous margins. The final frame matches official.png exactly. The only cost is the faint grey state at t=0.45.

X.top_fix: Replace the whole-logo opacity fade with motion built from the letterforms. For example, draw the word right-to-left along the baseline and let the dots land last, and cut the 2.6s static tail.

creative_originality.evidence: The motion follows how the script works. At t=0.45 a baseline stroke starts at the right edge, the start of the Arabic line, and the word is revealed right-to-left (t=0.88, t=1.33). The joins are stretched like a kashida (the word is about 585px wide at t=1.33 against about 400px in the final) and then contract by t=2.22. The dots are held back until the rasm skeleton is complete and arrive in reading order: the ta dots first, then the ya dots grey at t=2.22, then the qaf dots by t=2.65.

motion_quality.evidence: The sequence is well structured: stroke, skeleton, elongation, contraction, dots, then a hold from t=3.10 to t=3.98. There are two rough mid-states. At t=0.88 a detached bar floats far left of the partial letters. At t=0.88 and t=1.33 the qaf bowl is sliced flat at the bottom by the reveal mask, which reads as a clipping glitch. The dots only fade in grey (t=2.22) rather than dropping or snapping in with any weight.

brand_relevance.evidence: Writing the line right-to-left, stretching with kashida and adding the i'jam dots last suits an Arabic wordmark. It reads as a studio that builds the word rather than a template. The contraction at t=1.77 to t=2.22 gives a confident settle.

visual_clarity.evidence: The final frames (t=3.10 to t=3.98) are crisp, centred and identical to the official logo, with all joins and dots in place. During t=0.45 to t=1.77 the letters have no dots, so ta, ya and qaf read ambiguously and the word is hard to read for about 1.3s. At t=1.33 the stretched word nearly fills the frame width.

Y.top_fix: Fix the reveal mask so the qaf bowl and descender are never cut flat (t=0.88 and t=1.33), and remove the floating bar at t=0.88 by making the stroke grow from the letter it joins. Give the dots a short, snappy, slightly staggered drop-in instead of a plain grey fade.

why: X is a generic opacity fade that holds a static frame for about two thirds of its length and shows no awareness of the script. Y builds the word right-to-left, uses kashida elongation and brings the dots in last in reading order, so its movement comes from Arabic script behaviour. It has mask and floating-bar blemishes in mid-states, but it ends on the same clean, correctly joined and dotted logo as the official file. It is clearly the stronger piece.
